title: Design the Article catalogue card
description: Configure the six fields of the Article entity from the lesson. For each row pick the property name (lesson convention: camelCase in TS, snake_case in DB), the MikroORM type, and the right flag (PK, unique, nullable, default 0).

widgetConfig.prompt: Lesson 2's Article catalogue card. Pick name + type + flag for each row. The DB column names follow MikroORM's underscore naming strategy automatically.

modelAnswer: Article's spine in this course: bigint PK (room to grow past int's 2.1B ceiling), title varchar(200) NOT NULL, slug unique varchar, view_count int DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL, published_at timestamptz NULLABLE (drafts have no publish date), and metadata jsonb NULLABLE. The naming strategy maps camelCase TS to snake_case DB automatically — you write publishedAt, the column is published_at.

title: Fill in the Book entity definition

blanks.placeholder: DB modifier so the column is optional

modelAnswer: id: p.bigint().primary() — bigint, not integer, for headroom. title: p.string({ length: 200 }) — varchar(200), the course convention. publishedYear: p.integer().nullable() — the lesson hammers that .nullable() is the DB-side flag; the `?` in TypeScript is a separate concern.

title: Why does nullable (DB) not imply optional (TypeScript)?
description: Why does MikroORM require you to mark a property both .nullable() (for the database column) AND with '?' or '| null' in TypeScript (for the type system) separately — instead of inferring one from the other? What bad thing would happen if MikroORM auto-applied '| null' to every .nullable() column? Answer in 4-5 sentences.
modelAnswer: MikroORM separates the two so you can have a column that is NULL in storage but always present in the in-memory entity (because a service always fills it on load), or vice versa. Auto-applying `| null` would force every consumer of the entity to handle null even when business logic guarantees presence — flooding the codebase with non-null assertions or guards. The two flags answer two different questions: 'can the row be missing this value?' and 'can application code see undefined here?' Conflating them removes a useful expressive axis.
